questions.q_en: The speed of a boat in still water is 12 km/h, and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. A man goes to a place by boat, 45 km and comes back to the starting point. Find the total time taken by him.
questions.solution_en:
Speed of a boat in still water = 12 km/h

Speed of the stream = 3 km/h

Downstream speed = 12 + 3 = 15 km/h

Upstream speed = 12 - 3 = 9 km/h

Total time = 45/15 + 45/9 = 3 + 5 = 8 hours

questions.q_en: A vegetable vendor marks the price of carrots 30% above the cost price and offers an 18% discount to the customer. While purchasing, he measures 260 grams extra per kilogram, whereas during sales, he provides only 960 grams instead of 1 kg. Find his overall profit percentage. (rounded off to one decimal)
questions.solution_en:
Let cost price of carrots = ₹100

Marked price of carrots = 130% of 100 = ₹130

Discount = 18%

Selling price of carrots = (100 - 18)% of 130 = ₹106.6

Profit percentage = 6.6%

Now, He takes 1260 gm instead of 1000 gm and gives 960 gm instead of 1000 gm.

Profit = 1260 - 960 = 300

New cost price = ₹960

Profit % = (300/960)*100 = 31.25%

Overall profit percentage = 6.6 + 31.25 + (6.6*31.25)/100 = 39.9%

questions.q_en: Pipe A can fill a tank in 300 minutes while pipe B can empty the tank in 800 minutes. If pipe A opened for 120 minutes after that pipe B joined him for 80 minutes, then in how many hours the tank will be filled completely?
questions.solution_en:
Total capacity = LCM of 300 and 800 = 2400 units

Efficiency of pipe A = 2400/300 = 8 units/minutes

Efficiency of pipe B = 2400/800 = 3 units/minutes

Part filled by pipe A in 120 minutes = 120*8 = 960 units

Remaining units = 2400 - 960 = 1440 units

Part filled by pipe A and B together in 80 minutes = (8 - 3)*80 = 400 units

Remaining units = 1440 - 400 = 1040 units

Time taken by pipe A = 1040/8 = 130 minutes

Total time taken = 120 + 80 + 130 = 5.5 hours

questions.q_en: A hemispherical bowl is 88 cm round the brim. Assuming it to be full, how many persons may be served from it in hemispherical glasses, 7 cm in diameter at the top? (Where π = 22/7)
questions.solution_en:
Circumference of hemispherical bowl = 2πr = 88 cm

2 X (22/7) X r = 88

r = 88 X 7/44

r = 14 cm

Radius of hemispherical bowl = 7/2 = 3.5 cm

Number of glasses = (2/3 * π * 143) ÷ (2/3 * π * 3.53)

= (14/3.5)3

= 64

questions.q_en: Average number of boys in class P and Q is 45 and the average number of students in class P and Q is 64. If the number of girls in class P is 18, then find the ratio of the number of girls in class P to that in class Q.
questions.solution_en:
Number of boys in class P and Q = 2*45 = 90

Number of students in class P and Q = 2*64 = 128

Number of girls in class P = 18

Number of girls in class Q = 128 - 90 - 18 = 20

Required ratio = 18:20 = 9:10

Part filled by pipe A in a minute = 1/10

Part emptied by pipe B in a minute = 1/45

Part emptied by pipe C in a minute = 1/36

Time taken by all the pipes together to fill the tank = 1/(1/10 - 1/45 - 1/36) = 20 minutes

questions.q_en: From a point P outside the circle of center O, a tangent PT of length 12√3 cm is drawn. PBA is secant, radius of circle is 13 cm and perpendicular distance of chord AB from the center is 5 cm, then find the length of PA (PA > PB).
questions.solution_en:
PT = 12√3 cm

AO = 13 cm

OM = 5 cm

AM = √(AO2 - OM2) = √(132 - 52) = 12 cm

AB = 24 cm

We know that: PT2 = PA * PB

Let PB = 'x' cm

(12√3)2 = (x + 24) * x

x2 + 24x = 432

x2 + 24x - 432 = 0

x = 12

PA = x + 24 = 36 cm

questions.q_en: Emma and Jack each have a collection of pencils. If Emma gives one pencil to Jack, they will both have an equal number of pencils. Conversely, if Jack gives one pencil to Emma, she will end up with three times the number of pencils that Jack has. What is the total number of pencils they both have?
questions.solution_en:
Let the number of pencils Emma has be X, and the number of pencils jack has be Y.

Given that

X - 1 = Y + 1

X - Y = 2 ... (1)

And

(X + 1) = 3(Y - 1)

X + 1 = 3Y - 3

X - 3Y = -4

3Y - X = 4 ... (2)

After solving equations (1) and (2),

Y = 3 and X = 5

Total number of pencils Emma and Jack have is 8.

questions.q_en: For a certain article, if discount is 22% the profit is 17%. If the discount is 12%, then the profit is:
questions.solution_en:
Let marked price of article = Rs.100

Selling price of article = 100 * 78/100 = Rs.78

Profit% = 17%

Cost price of article = 100 * 78/(100 + 17)

= 100 * 78/117 = 100 * 2/3 = Rs.200/3

If the discount is 12%, then selling price will be = 100 * 88/100 = Rs.88

Profit% = [88 - (200/3)] * 100/(200/3) = 64 * 100/200 = 32%.

questions.q_en: In a company of a certain number of employees, if one employee weighing 56 kg is added, then the average weight of the employees increases by 1 kg. If one more employee weighing 52.4 kg is added, then the average weight of the employees increases by 1.2 kg over the original average. What is the original average weight of the employees?
questions.solution_en:
Let total number of employees = n

Average weight = w kg

Now,

(nw + 56) = (n + 1)(w + 1)

n + w = 55 -------(1)

(nw + 56 + 52.4) = (n + 2)(w + 1.2)

1.2n + 2w = 106 ------(2)

From (1) and (2) -

n = 5, w = 50

Original average weight of the employees = 50 kg

questions.q_en: A can complete a certain work in 35 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They worked together for 7 days, then B left the work. In how many days will A alone complete 60% of the remaining work?
questions.solution_en:
Let total work = LCM of 35 and 15 = 105 units

Part of work done by A in 1 day = 105/35 = 3 units

Part of work done by B in 1 day = 105/15 = 7 units

Total work done by A and B together in 7 days = 7 * (3 + 7) = 70 units

Remaining work = 105 - 70 = 35 units

Time taken by A alone to complete 60% of remaining work = (60% of 35)/3

= 7 days
